newsitem.title: IRAQ: GAMES-IRAQ CONDEMNS LEBANON'S DECISION TO BAR ATHLETES.
newsitem.headline: GAMES-IRAQ CONDEMNS LEBANON'S DECISION TO BAR ATHLETES.

text.p: Iraq on Wednesday condemned a Lebanese decision to exclude Iraqi athletes from the Pan Arab Games.
"Taking such an unjust decision against an Arab country...does not represent the will of Arab people," the newspaper of the ruling Baath party al-Thawra said.
The paper said that even the United States, which led the 1991 Gulf War against Iraq, had not prevented Iraqi athletes from taking part in the 1996 Atlanta Olympics.

Lebanon severed diplomatic ties with Baghdad in 1994 after the murder of an Iraqi dissident in Beirut and sources at the Games, which open in Beirut on Saturday, said on Tuesday no visas would be issued to the Iraqis.
Al-Thawra said: "Iraq will not lose anything for not participating in the Games because it is not after winning, rather it views the Games as representing a brotherly meeting."
Gulf Arab states -- Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Bahrain and Oman -- had threatened to boycott the Games if Iraq participated, a source at the Games said.
Kuwait, still haunted by memories of the 1990 Iraqi invasion of their tiny oil-rich state, made their boycott threat last month after Iraq had confirmed their participation.
